A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POGEMA benchmark. The complete documents, including appendices A–J in v1 and A–L in v2, support comparison. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable, and renamed datasets and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of MARL, hybrid and centralized solvers on MAPF and lifelong MAPF tasks, with numerical results in Section 4.3 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V2 retains and revises the solver evaluations and adds original environment-speed, parallel-sampling and large-agent-population measurements in Appendix L.

M1.justification: The proposed environment retains its transition mechanics, collision shielding, observation tensors, rewards and MAPF/LMAPF procedures in Section 3. Baseline tuning and revised evaluation metrics change the experiments, while the added map-ingestion utility supports data preparation.

E1.justification: The six benchmark map families and two pathfinding tasks remain; Cities and Cities-tiles match the earlier MovingAI subsets, including Table 3 settings. Appendix L extends stress-test coverage to 3072×3072 random maps with up to one million agents and 128×128 lifelong mazes with Follower and up to 2048 agents.

E2.justification: Corresponding MAPF and LMAPF comparisons retain the same named solver sets. V2 newly specifies LaCAM-v3, but v1 leaves its implementation version unspecified, so replacement is not established. Appendix L quotes EnvPool and JaxMARL performance rather than reporting newly conducted evaluations of those comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 replaces density-based Congestion with collision-based Coordination and changes Pathfinding from binary optimality to a path-cost ratio. Appendix H changes the stated protocol from default hyperparameters to grid-search tuning for IQL, QPLEX, QMIX and VDN. Appendix L introduces controlled CPU, worker-count, population-size and policy-dependent timing experiments.

E4.justification: Warehouse congestion-density analyses are removed and replaced by collision analyses on Random and Mazes maps in Appendices B.6 and C.6. New Appendix L investigates hardware dependence, parallel-sampling overhead, extreme population scaling and environment throughput under Follower instead of only random actions, substantially expanding supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same evaluation seed counts. Both versions use 95% confidence bands and interval reporting for solver results, without documenting a changed estimation procedure or increased training repetitions. Changed interval values accompany revised results; the new speed measurements introduce no new uncertainty-reporting method.

E6.justification: Many solver results and rankings change. QPLEX's 256-agent lifelong out-of-distribution throughput changes from 1.74±0.11 to 4.22±0.22 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 6), accompanying revised training rather than establishing a same-setting gain. LaCAM's Table 4 CSR changes from 0.96 to 1.00. V2 reports QPLEX instead of MAMBA as the leading lifelong MARL method and adds collision and extensive speed results while removing congestion results.

T1.justification: There are localized changes to formal metric definitions: Equation 8 replaces the congestion density ratio with 1 minus collisions divided by agent-steps, and Equation 9 replaces binary path optimality with a path-cost ratio and zero for failure. These are mathematical revisions, but no new theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central contribution: a unified fast environment, instance generation, visualization, automated benchmarking and domain-specific evaluation for MARL, hybrid and planning methods. The change from navigation to pathfinding terminology aligns the framing with the already evaluated MAPF/LMAPF problems.

C2.justification: V1 characterizes MARL methods as underperforming in lifelong scenarios; v2 says they can compete with hybrid methods and links this to Follower's observation model. V2 also attributes MAMBA's strengths to communication, adds explanations involving collision avoidance and action masking, and discusses CPU/GPU simulation tradeoffs and random-policy timing limitations. The original communication and JAX limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds selected hyperparameters in Table 9, baseline implementation and checkpoint links in Appendix A, explicit identification of Mazes training maps, and detailed hardware and sampling settings in Appendix L. Appendix K provides MovingAI-to-YAML ingestion code and access instructions. Repository links are updated; much of the earlier configuration and resource documentation is retained.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning around classical MAPF algorithms and transferring discrete plans to physical robots, replacing much of the general MARL-challenges discussion. New references cover search, SAT, rule-based planning and kinematic constraints. Table 1 and Appendix F add substantive comparisons with MAGent and Gigastep, while the MovingAI source receives an explicit citation.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list and results narrative undergo substantial rewriting. Related-work explanations are consolidated, terminology is standardized, the conclusion gains a future-work discussion, and two appendix sections are added. These narrative changes extend beyond the conference header, author formatting and citation-style conversion.

P2.justification: V2 redraws and reorders radar-chart axes, replaces congestion tables with collision plots, and adds hyperparameter and speed tables, worker-scaling heatmaps and throughput curves. Existing code listings become boxed figures, while the conference layout relocates the abstract, teaser and several tables. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Tuning previously default MARL baselines and documenting selected settings strengthens the comparisons, while Appendix L directly tests platform-speed and scalability claims. Additional implementation and map-ingestion information improves reproducibility. These gains are tempered by introduced inconsistencies: Equation 9 prints path_cost/path_costoptimal despite stating that paths closer to optimal receive higher scores, and Appendix B.4 still reports LaCAM CSR as 0.96 although the updated Table 4 gives 1.00. The net improvement is therefore limited.
